intelligence.human_view: "I'm going to keep telling you" is the sentence that says the lesson has not landed — the machine keeps breaking a law it already holds, so he has to say it again. Every page making new icons is how one system becomes ten styles: the sidebar drifts, the bar drifts, the look drifts, and nothing feels like the same place. The 18:33Z law covered only the bar; this one covers everything — every icon, every sidebar, the whole look and feel. One set, one sidebar, one look: the same ones, everywhere, so every page feels like the same world. And the enforcement is blunt, by his own words: a round that makes a new icon for its page has failed.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine every room in your house had different light switches — a new kind in every room! You'd never know how to turn the lights on. From now on, every room gets the SAME switches, the SAME look — so everywhere feels like home.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, every page has been making its own new icons, and it makes the whole place feel different everywhere you go. From now on, the same icons on every page, the same sidebar, the same look and feel — not different styles, the same ones.
intelligence.naya_view: ONE ICON SET, ONE SIDEBAR, ONE LOOK — EVERY PAGE. STOP MAKING NEW ICONS FOR EVERY PAGE. THE SAME ICONS ON EVERY PAGE. THE SAME SIDEBARS ON EVERY PAGE. THE SAME LOOK AND FEEL ON EVERY PAGE. NOT DIFFERENT STYLES — THE SAME ONES. A ROUND THAT MAKES A NEW ICON FOR ITS PAGE HAS FAILED.
